ownership_history.event: Winterfell is founded after the Long Night.
Torrhen Stark, the King Who Knelt, bends the knee to Aegon the Conqueror.
Lord Ellard Stark supports Laenor Velaryon's claim at the Great Council of 101 AC.
Cregan Stark forms the Pact of Ice and Fire with Prince Jacaerys Velaryon, later marching south in the Hour of the Wolf.
Lord Beron Stark gathers troops to defend the northern coastlines against Dagon Greyjoy's raids.
Lord Rickard Stark is brutally executed by King Aerys II in King's Landing.
Lord Eddard Stark returns to Winterfell with his infant son Robb Stark after Robert's Rebellion.
King Robert I visits Winterfell. Eddard Stark leaves to become Hand of the King.
Winterfell is captured by Theon Greyjoy, then betrayed and burned by Ramsay Snow.
House Bolton seizes control of the North. Roose Bolton occupies the ruined Winterfell.

metadata.description: The ancient seat of House Stark, a vast stronghold built thousands of years ago in the heart of the North. It stands above hot springs that heat its halls.
metadata.narratorText: Winterfell is the capital of the North. Built by Brandon the Builder in the Age of Heroes, the castle is protected by double granite walls and a deep moat. Below the castle lie the Crypts of Winterfell, where the Kings of Winter are laid to rest with stone direwolves and iron swords.

timeline.event: Winterfell is founded after the Long Night.
Torrhen Stark, the King Who Knelt, bends the knee to Aegon the Conqueror.
Lord Ellard Stark supports Laenor Velaryon's claim at the Great Council of 101 AC.
Cregan Stark forms the Pact of Ice and Fire with Prince Jacaerys Velaryon, later marching south in the Hour of the Wolf.
Lord Beron Stark gathers troops to defend the northern coastlines against Dagon Greyjoy's raids.
Lord Rickard Stark is brutally executed by King Aerys II in King's Landing.

King Robert I visits Winterfell. Eddard Stark leaves to become Hand of the King.
Winterfell is captured by Theon Greyjoy, then betrayed and burned by Ramsay Snow.
House Bolton seizes control of the North. Roose Bolton occupies the ruined Winterfell.

ownership_history.event: The Night's Watch guards the Wall under Targaryen rule.
Lord Commander Jack Musgood, known as Jolly Jack, is outgeneraled by Raymun Redbeard, who leads a wildling host across the Wall.
Lord Commander Jeor Mormont prepares the Great Ranger Mutiny beyond the Wall, where he is eventually murdered.
Jon Snow is elected the 998th Lord Commander of the Night's Watch after the battle at Castle Black.

metadata.description: The primary headquarters of the Night's Watch, situated at the center of the Wall. It has no walls of its own, only the massive ice barrier to its north.
metadata.narratorText: Castle Black is the largest of the castles along the Wall. In Year 1 AC, it is ruled by Lord Commander Tristan Mudd, guarding the realm of men against wildlings and worse.

timeline.event: The Night's Watch guards the Wall under Targaryen rule.
Lord Commander Jack Musgood, known as Jolly Jack, is outgeneraled by Raymun Redbeard, who leads a wildling host across the Wall.
Lord Commander Jeor Mormont prepares the Great Ranger Mutiny beyond the Wall, where he is eventually murdered.
Jon Snow is elected the 998th Lord Commander of the Night's Watch after the battle at Castle Black.

ownership_history.event: Eastwatch-by-the-Sea functions as the primary port for the Night's Watch.
Queen Alysanne Targaryen visits the Wall; the Eastwatch fleet patrols the Bay of Seals.
Eastwatch patrols coordinate with Stark ships to intercept wildling smugglers.
Cotter Pyke is Commander of Eastwatch, monitoring wildling movements by sea.
King Stannis Baratheon arrives at Eastwatch with his fleet to assist the Night's Watch.

metadata.description: The easternmost castle on the Wall, acting as a port for the Night's Watch to monitor trade and wildling movements across the Bay of Seals.
metadata.narratorText: Eastwatch-by-the-Sea is critical for the trade and naval operations of the Night's Watch. It prevents wildling smugglers from landing south of the Wall.

timeline.event: Eastwatch-by-the-Sea functions as the primary port for the Night's Watch.
Queen Alysanne Targaryen visits the Wall; the Eastwatch fleet patrols the Bay of Seals.
Eastwatch patrols coordinate with Stark ships to intercept wildling smugglers.
Cotter Pyke is Commander of Eastwatch, monitoring wildling movements by sea.
King Stannis Baratheon arrives at Eastwatch with his fleet to assist the Night's Watch.

ownership_history.event: The Shadow Tower guards the western gorge of the Wall.
Watchmen patrol the dangerous mountain passes of the western reaches.
Rangers from the Shadow Tower report increased wildling activity in the Frostfangs.
Ser Denys Mallister is appointed Commander of the Shadow Tower.
The Shadow Tower scouts fight wildling raiders at the Gorge.

metadata.description: A dark fortress built into the cliffs near the western gorge of the Wall, guarding the hazardous mountain passes of the Frostfangs.
metadata.narratorText: Perched precariously on the mountain cliffs, the Shadow Tower guards the western reach of the Wall, where the gorge offers passage to wildling raiders.

timeline.event: The Shadow Tower guards the western gorge of the Wall.
Watchmen patrol the dangerous mountain passes of the western reaches.
Rangers from the Shadow Tower report increased wildling activity in the Frostfangs.
Ser Denys Mallister is appointed Commander of the Shadow Tower.
The Shadow Tower scouts fight wildling raiders at the Gorge.

ownership_history.event: Loren Lannister submits to Aegon I after the Field of Fire and is named Warden of the West.
Lord Jason Lannister supports the Greens in the Dance of the Dragons, marching his host to the Riverlands.
Following Jason's death, Lady Johanna Lannister rules as regent, successfully defending Casterly Rock and the West from the Red Kraken.
Lord Damon Lannister, the Grey Lion, rules Casterly Rock during the First Blackfyre Rebellion.
Lord Tywin Lannister serves as Lord of Casterly Rock and Warden of the West, expanding the family's immense wealth and power.
Following Tywin Lannister's murder, his daughter Queen Regent Cersei Lannister becomes Lady of Casterly Rock.

metadata.description: A colossal fortress carved out of a massive stone mount overlooking the Sunset Sea, served as the wealthy seat of House Lannister.
metadata.narratorText: Casterly Rock is carved from a stone hill resembling a couchant lion. It contains massive gold veins, making House Lannister the richest family in Westeros. Its tunnels, halls, and dungeons stretch deep underground.

timeline.event: Loren Lannister submits to Aegon I after the Field of Fire and is named Warden of the West.
Lord Jason Lannister supports the Greens in the Dance of the Dragons, marching his host to the Riverlands.
Following Jason's death, Lady Johanna Lannister rules as regent, successfully defending Casterly Rock and the West from the Red Kraken.
Lord Damon Lannister, the Grey Lion, rules Casterly Rock during the First Blackfyre Rebellion.
Lord Tywin Lannister serves as Lord of Casterly Rock and Warden of the West, expanding the family's immense wealth and power.
Following Tywin Lannister's murder, his daughter Queen Regent Cersei Lannister becomes Lady of Casterly Rock.

ownership_history.event: Queen Regent Sharra Arryn yields the Eyrie after Visenya Targaryen flies Vhagar directly into the courtyard.
Lady Jeyne Arryn, the Maiden of the Vale, aligns House Arryn with Queen Rhaenyra and the Blacks.
Lord Jon Arryn raises the banners of the Vale in rebellion after Aerys II demands the heads of Eddard Stark and Robert Baratheon.
Following Jon Arryn's death, Lady Lysa Arryn flees to the Eyrie with her son Robert Arryn and maintains neutrality.
Lysa Arryn is pushed to her death from the Moon Door. Lord Petyr Baelish seizes control as Lord Protector of the Vale.

metadata.description: An impregnable fortress perched high atop the Giant's Lance mountain, accessible only by a narrow mountain path guarded by three waycastles.
metadata.narratorText: Perched six thousand feet above the Vale, the Eyrie is the smallest of the great castles, consisting of seven slim white towers. Its height makes it impregnable to assault, but Queen Visenya Targaryen bypassed all defenses by flying her dragon Vhagar straight to the top.

timeline.event: Queen Regent Sharra Arryn yields the Eyrie after Visenya Targaryen flies Vhagar directly into the courtyard.
Lady Jeyne Arryn, the Maiden of the Vale, aligns House Arryn with Queen Rhaenyra and the Blacks.

ownership_history.event: Aenar Targaryen sells his estates in Valyria and moves his family to Dragonstone.
Dragonstone remains the primary stronghold and seat of House Targaryen.
Aenys I Targaryen succeeds Aegon I and inherits Dragonstone.
Dowager Queen Visenya Targaryen seizes control of Dragonstone and crowns Maegor I Targaryen.
Jaehaerys I Targaryen makes Dragonstone his temporary seat before reconciling with the Faith.
Rhaenyra Targaryen is crowned Queen at Dragonstone, making it the capital of the Blacks.
Aegon II Targaryen secretly takes Dragonstone and executes Rhaenyra by feeding her to his dragon Sunfyre.
Stannis Baratheon captures Dragonstone, ending Targaryen presence, and Robert grants him the seat.
Stannis declares himself King and rallies his vassals at Dragonstone.

metadata.description: The volcanic island fortress built by the Valyrian Freehold using advanced stonemasonry, serving as the ancestral seat of House Targaryen.
metadata.narratorText: Dragonstone was shaped by Valyrian dragonlords using magic and fire to warp stone into the shapes of dragons and gargoyles. It is a grim, black fortress sitting in the shadow of the volcano Dragonmont.

timeline.event: Aenar Targaryen sells his estates in Valyria and moves his family to Dragonstone.
Dragonstone remains the primary stronghold and seat of House Targaryen.

ownership_history.event: Aegon lands at the mouth of the Blackwater and erects a crude fort of wood and earth.
The Aegonfort is expanded as stone buildings start to rise, founding King's Landing.
Aenys I Targaryen succeeds Aegon I. Construction of the Red Keep begins.
Maegor I Targaryen seizes the Iron Throne after the death of Aenys I.
The Red Keep is completed. Maegor executes all the builders to hide the castle's secret passages.
Maegor I dies on the Iron Throne. Jaehaerys I Targaryen succeeds him.
King Jaehaerys I Targaryen dies. Viserys I Targaryen succeeds him peacefully.
Aegon II Targaryen seizes the throne, sparking the Dance of the Dragons.
Queen Rhaenyra Targaryen captures King's Landing and sits on the Iron Throne.
Aegon II Targaryen is poisoned. Aegon III Targaryen succeeds him under regency.
King Aegon III dies. His son Daeron I Targaryen, the Young Dragon, succeeds him.
Daeron I Targaryen is killed in Dorne. Baelor I Targaryen succeeds him.
Aegon IV Targaryen (the Unworthy) ascends the Iron Throne.
Aegon IV Targaryen dies. Daeron II Targaryen succeeds him.
Daeron II dies of the Great Spring Sickness. Aerys I Targaryen succeeds him.
Maekar I Targaryen succeeds Aerys I on the Iron Throne.
Maekar I dies in battle. The Great Council elects Aegon V Targaryen (Egg).
Aegon V dies at Summerhall. Jaehaerys II Targaryen succeeds him.
Aerys II Targaryen succeeds Jaehaerys II on the Iron Throne.
Tywin Lannister sacks the city. Aerys II is slain, and Robert Baratheon claims the throne.
Robert Baratheon dies. Joffrey Baratheon ascends the Iron Throne.
Joffrey is poisoned. Tommen Baratheon succeeds him.

metadata.description: Initially the Aegonfort, a rough wood-and-earth fort built at the mouth of the Blackwater Rush where Aegon first landed. Now transforming into the new capital city.
metadata.narratorText: In Year 1 AC, King's Landing is a muddy, sprawling settlement growing around the Aegonfort. Aegon I Targaryen has chosen this spot as his capital, ordering the construction of a city that will house the Iron Throne.

Joffrey is poisoned. Tommen Baratheon succeeds him.

ownership_history.event: Harlan Tyrell yields Highgarden to Aegon I after King Mern IX Gardener dies on the Field of Fire. Aegon grants him the castle.
The infant Lord Tyrell's mother serves as regent, maintaining neutrality for Highgarden during the Dance of the Dragons.
Lord Mace Tyrell rules Highgarden, leading the Reach's vast military host during Robert's Rebellion.
Highgarden allies with Renly Baratheon, betrothing Margaery Tyrell to him.

metadata.description: A breathtaking tiered castle surrounded by briar labyrinths, orchards, and white stone walls, overlooking the placid waters of the Mander.
metadata.narratorText: Highgarden is the seat of the Lords Paramount of the Reach. Formerly held by House Gardener, it was given to House Tyrell, their stewards, after the Field of Fire, which caused great resentment among older Reach houses.

timeline.event: Harlan Tyrell yields Highgarden to Aegon I after King Mern IX Gardener dies on the Field of Fire. Aegon grants him the castle.
The infant Lord Tyrell's mother serves as regent, maintaining neutrality for Highgarden during the Dance of the Dragons.

Highgarden allies with Renly Baratheon, betrothing Margaery Tyrell to him.

ownership_history.event: Edmyn Tully leads the rebel river lords to join Aegon I and is named Lord Paramount of the Trident.
Lord Grover Tully wishes to support the Greens, but his grandson Elmo Tully holds the castle for the Blacks.
Young Lord Kermit Tully leads the Riverlords to victory at the Battle of the Kingsroad.
Lord Hoster Tully joins Robert's Rebellion, marrying his daughters to Jon Arryn and Eddard Stark.
Jaime Lannister defeats Edmure Tully outside Riverrun and lays siege to the castle.
The Tullies are stripped of Riverrun, which is granted to Emmon Frey by the Iron Throne.

metadata.description: A stout stone castle situated at the confluence of the Tumblestone and Red Fork. Its unique design allows it to be surrounded by water on all three sides.
metadata.narratorText: Riverrun's strategic design allows its defenders to open sluice gates, flooding a wide moat and turning the castle into an island that cannot be breached. Edmyn Tully rebelled against King Harren the Black, winning Aegon's favor.

timeline.event: Edmyn Tully leads the rebel river lords to join Aegon I and is named Lord Paramount of the Trident.

ownership_history.event: Harren the Black completes construction of Harrenhal after forty years of slave labor.
Aegon I Targaryen grants the ruined and melted Harrenhal to Lucas Qoherys, former master-at-arms of Dragonstone.
Gargon Qoherys is killed by rebel Harren the Red. King Aenys I grants Harrenhal to Lucas Harroway.
Maegor I Targaryen exterminates House Harroway. He grants the ruined castle to House Towers.
Lord Maegor Towers dies without heirs. Jaehaerys I grants Harrenhal to Lyonel Strong. Great Council of 101 meets here.
Daemon Targaryen captures Harrenhal for the Blacks. Ser Aemond later executes all of House Strong except Larys.
King Aegon III grants Harrenhal to Lucas Lothston.
House Whent holds the great Tourney of Harrenhal, where Prince Rhaegar meets Lyanna Stark.
Lady Shella Whent yields Harrenhal to Lord Tywin Lannister during the War of the Five Kings.

metadata.description: The largest castle ever built in Westeros, now a half-melted black ruin after Aegon Targaryen unleashed Balerion's dragonfire to destroy Harren the Black.
metadata.narratorText: Harrenhal's colossal towers were melted like wax when Balerion bathed the castle in dragonfire. In Year 1 AC, it stands as a terrifying monument to the power of the Targaryen dragons, left empty and haunted.

Lady Shella Whent yields Harrenhal to Lord Tywin Lannister during the War of the Five Kings.

ownership_history.event: Vickon Greyjoy is elected by the ironborn to rule the Iron Islands from Pyke after Aegon I executes the Hoare pretenders.
Dalton Greyjoy, the Red Kraken, becomes Lord of the Iron Islands. He aligns with the Blacks and attacks the Westerlands.
Balon Greyjoy declares himself King of the Iron Islands. Pyke is besieged and breached by King Robert and Lord Stark. Balon yields.
Balon Greyjoy declares independence once more and launches attacks on the North during the War of the Five Kings.
Balon falls from a bridge to his death. His exiled brother Euron Greyjoy seizes Pyke and the Seastone Chair.

metadata.description: An ancient stronghold built on jagged rock stacks jutting into the sea, connected by swaying rope and wood bridges.
metadata.narratorText: Pyke is the ancient seat of House Greyjoy. Over centuries, the cliffs have eroded into the sea, leaving the castle towers standing on isolated stone spires lashed by the salt water.

timeline.event: Vickon Greyjoy is elected by the ironborn to rule the Iron Islands from Pyke after Aegon I executes the Hoare pretenders.
Dalton Greyjoy, the Red Kraken, becomes Lord of the Iron Islands. He aligns with the Blacks and attacks the Westerlands.
Balon Greyjoy declares himself King of the Iron Islands. Pyke is besieged and breached by King Robert and Lord Stark. Balon yields.
Balon Greyjoy declares independence once more and launches attacks on the North during the War of the Five Kings.
Balon falls from a bridge to his death. His exiled brother Euron Greyjoy seizes Pyke and the Seastone Chair.

ownership_history.event: Orys Baratheon slays King Argilac Durrandon, marries his daughter Argella, and is granted the castle and lands by Aegon I.
Lord Borros Baratheon receives Aemond Targaryen and aligns House Baratheon with Aegon II and the Greens.
Stannis Baratheon holds Storm's End through a year-long siege by the Tyrell host, saved from starvation by Davos Seaworth.
King Robert grants the ancestral seat of Storm's End to his youngest brother Renly Baratheon.
Renly Baratheon claims the Iron Throne and gathers his massive host at Storm's End.
Renly is assassinated. Ser Cortnay Penrose refuses to yield, is killed, and Stannis Baratheon seizes the fortress.

metadata.description: An ancient, massive fortress built by Durran Godsgrief. Its single colossal drum tower is protected by a shield wall that repels the storms of Shipbreaker Bay.
metadata.narratorText: Storm's End is said to have magic woven into its stones to prevent spells from crossing its walls. Its massive curtain wall is eighty feet thick, designed to withstand the fury of Shipbreaker Bay.

timeline.event: Orys Baratheon slays King Argilac Durrandon, marries his daughter Argella, and is granted the castle and lands by Aegon I.
Lord Borros Baratheon receives Aemond Targaryen and aligns House Baratheon with Aegon II and the Greens.

King Robert grants the ancestral seat of Storm's End to his youngest brother Renly Baratheon.
Renly Baratheon claims the Iron Throne and gathers his massive host at Storm's End.
Renly is assassinated. Ser Cortnay Penrose refuses to yield, is killed, and Stannis Baratheon seizes the fortress.

ownership_history.event: Princess Meria Martell resists Aegon's Conquest, keeping Dorne independent.
King Daeron I conquers Dorne. Sunspear yields and bends the knee, though Dornish resistance continues.
Dorne rebels and kills Daeron's regent. Baelor I walks barefoot to Sunspear to forge peace, restoring Dornish independence.
Prince Maron Martell marries Daenerys Targaryen, joining Dorne to the Seven Kingdoms peacefully.
Prince Doran Martell rules Dorne from Sunspear, keeping his realm isolated from the War of the Five Kings.

metadata.description: A sprawling castle of mudbrick and gold domes located on the dry eastern coast of Dorne. The seat of the independent House Martell.
metadata.narratorText: Sunspear consists of the Spear Tower and the Tower of the Sun, rising above the sprawling Shadow City. In Year 1 AC, it remains the only sovereign palace in Westeros, refusing to yield to Targaryen dragons.

timeline.event: Princess Meria Martell resists Aegon's Conquest, keeping Dorne independent.

ownership_history.event: House Manderly swears fealty to Winterfell and builds up White Harbor.
Lord Desmond Manderly welcomes Jacaerys Velaryon and pledges support to the Blacks.
Medrick Manderly rules White Harbor, maintaining trade relations.
Lord Wyman Manderly succeeds his father and joins Robert's Rebellion.
Lord Wyman fortifies White Harbor and secretly constructs a massive fleet.

metadata.description: The New Keep is the castle of House Manderly, overlooking the wealthy port city of White Harbor on the Knife river.
metadata.narratorText: White Harbor is the only true city in the North. House Manderly, originally exiled from the Reach, built the New Keep here and guards the North's eastern trade.

timeline.event: House Manderly swears fealty to Winterfell and builds up White Harbor.
Lord Desmond Manderly welcomes Jacaerys Velaryon and pledges support to the Blacks.
Medrick Manderly rules White Harbor, maintaining trade relations.
Lord Wyman Manderly succeeds his father and joins Robert's Rebellion.
Lord Wyman fortifies White Harbor and secretly constructs a massive fleet.

ownership_history.event: Manfred Hightower opens the gates to Aegon the Conqueror, who is crowned here.
Lord Martyn Hightower succeeds his brother and resolves conflicts with the Faith.
Lord Ormund Hightower supports Aegon II and the Greens during the Dance.
House Hightower oversees a period of quiet prosperity in Oldtown.
Lord Leyton Hightower, the Voice of Oldtown, rules from the Hightower.
Lord Leyton remains in the tower preparing defenses against Euron Greyjoy's fleet.

metadata.description: A colossal stone lighthouse that serves as the seat of House Hightower, rising hundreds of feet over the harbor of Oldtown.
metadata.narratorText: The Hightower is the tallest structure in the known world, topped by a beacon fire. In Year 1 AC, it towers over Oldtown, the center of learning (the Citadel) and the Faith in Westeros.

timeline.event: Manfred Hightower opens the gates to Aegon the Conqueror, who is crowned here.
Lord Martyn Hightower succeeds his brother and resolves conflicts with the Faith.

Lord Leyton Hightower, the Voice of Oldtown, rules from the Hightower.

ownership_history.event: Torrhen Stark gathers his army at Moat Cailin before marching south.
Cregan Stark gathers the northern hosts at Moat Cailin before marching south.
Northern forces stand ready at Moat Cailin during times of wildling threat.
Robb Stark commands the crannogmen and his archers to secure the three towers.
Victarion Greyjoy captures the ruined fortress for House Greyjoy, blocking the Neck.
Ramsay Bolton uses Theon to trick the ironborn garrison into yielding.

metadata.description: An ancient, decaying fortress consisting of three basalt towers guarding the Neck. It is the key to defending the North from southern invasion.
metadata.narratorText: Though mostly ruined, Moat Cailin's positioning in the swamps of the Neck makes it impossible to take from the south. Its towers command the only passable road into the North.

timeline.event: Torrhen Stark gathers his army at Moat Cailin before marching south.
Cregan Stark gathers the northern hosts at Moat Cailin before marching south.

ownership_history.event: House Bolton reluctantly submits to Torrhen Stark's peace with the Targaryens.
Lord Roose Bolton rules the Dreadfort and fights at the Battle of the Trident under Eddard Stark.
Ramsay Snow sacks Winterfell and is legitimized as Ramsay Bolton. The Boltons betray the Starks at the Red Wedding.
Roose Bolton is named Warden of the North by the Iron Throne, ruling from Winterfell.

metadata.description: A sinister, thick-walled fortress located on the Weeping Water, the ancestral seat of House Bolton, long-time rivals of the Starks.
metadata.narratorText: The Dreadfort is notorious for its dark history of flaying enemies, a practice House Bolton officially abandoned when they swore fealty to Winterfell, though rumors persist.

timeline.event: House Bolton reluctantly submits to Torrhen Stark's peace with the Targaryens.
Lord Roose Bolton rules the Dreadfort and fights at the Battle of the Trident under Eddard Stark.

ownership_history.event: House Frey extracts tolls from travelers crossing the Trident.
Forrest Frey (the Fool) joins the Blacks and leads Frey levies to battle during the Dance of the Dragons.
Walder Frey, the Late Lord Frey, arrives too late to the Battle of the Trident during Robert's Rebellion.
House Frey hosts the Red Wedding, murdering King Robb Stark and violating guest right.

metadata.description: Two identical fortresses flanking the Green Fork of the Trident, connected by a heavily fortified stone bridge. Seat of House Frey.
metadata.narratorText: The Twins control the strategic crossing of the Green Fork. Built over generations by House Frey, the bridge and its twin towers represent immense wealth and transit control.

timeline.event: White Harbor handles silver and timber exports for Winterfell.

ownership_history.event: Gulltown harbor expands shipping lanes to Bravos.

metadata.description: A wealthy merchant city situated on the Bay of Crabs, acting as the primary window of the Vale to the rest of the world.
metadata.narratorText: Sworn to House Grafton, Gulltown is a key trading hub. During the Conquest, a naval battle was fought in its harbor, resulting in the destruction of the Targaryen fleet and the death of Daemon Velaryon.

timeline.event: Gulltown harbor expands shipping lanes to Bravos.

ownership_history.event: Planky Town trades with Free Cities, bypassing Targaryen waters.

metadata.description: A floating merchant town at the mouth of the Greenblood river, where houseboats and rafts are tied together to form a colorful marketplace.
metadata.narratorText: Planky Town is Dorne's gateway to the world. Orphans of the Greenblood navigate their barges here to sell spices, citrus fruits, and fine silk to foreign merchants.

timeline.event: Planky Town trades with Free Cities, bypassing Targaryen waters.

ownership_history.event: Barrowton levies swear fealty to the Starks.

metadata.description: A large town built around the Great Barrow of the First Kings, ruled by House Dustin.
metadata.narratorText: Barrowton is a unique northern town with wooden streets and houses clustered around a colossal earthen hill where ancient kings are said to sleep.

timeline.event: Barrowton levies swear fealty to the Starks.

ownership_history.event: Stoney Sept submits to Targaryen control.

metadata.description: A prosperous walled market town in the southern Riverlands, named for its massive stone sept.
metadata.narratorText: Stoney Sept is a major trade crossroads in the heart of the Riverlands. Its stone walls and towering sept make it a local fortress.

timeline.event: Stoney Sept submits to Targaryen control.

ownership_history.event: Duskendale yields to Targaryen rule during initial conquest.

metadata.description: An ancient port town on the Narrow Sea, ruled by House Rykker, serving as a vital anchorage for coastal shipping.
metadata.narratorText: Prior to the rise of King's Landing, Duskendale was the primary port on the Blackwater bay, generating immense customs revenue from seafaring trade.

timeline.event: Duskendale yields to Targaryen rule during initial conquest.

ownership_history.event: House Mooton submits to Aegon I.

metadata.description: An ancient walled town on the southern shores of the Bay of Crabs, ruled by House Mooton and famous for Jonquil's Pool.
metadata.narratorText: Maidenpool is named for Jonquil's Pool, where the legendary Jonquil was found bathing by Florian the Fool. It is a vital hub for fishing and trade.

timeline.event: House Mooton submits to Aegon I.

ownership_history.event: Saltpans ships salt and salted fish to King's Landing.

metadata.description: A small port town at the mouth of the Trident, famous for its salt pans which supply the Riverlands.
metadata.narratorText: Saltpans is critical for preserving food in Westeros. Its shallow evaporative pans create high-quality salt traded far and wide.

timeline.event: Saltpans ships salt and salted fish to King's Landing.

ownership_history.event: Harroway ferry resumes normal operations under Tully control.

metadata.description: A town located where the Kingsroad crosses the Trident via ferry, named for the ancient House Harroway.
metadata.narratorText: Lord Harroway's Town is a crucial bottleneck on the Kingsroad. It sits on low ground and is subject to frequent flooding when the Trident rises.

timeline.event: Harroway ferry resumes normal operations under Tully control.

ownership_history.event: The Wall is constructed to defend the realms of men.

metadata.description: A colossal barrier of solid ice, stone, and ancient magic, stretching 300 miles from the Gorge to the Bay of Seals. It stands over 700 feet tall.
metadata.narratorText: The Wall is the legendary shield of the Seven Kingdoms. Built with ice and reinforced with old runes, it is guarded by the Night's Watch, who staff several castles along its base.

timeline.event: The Wall is constructed to defend the realms of men.

metadata.description: The largest lake in Westeros, containing deep, mysterious waters and acting as the southern border of Harrenhal.
metadata.narratorText: The God's Eye is a sacred body of water, steeped in history. The Pact between the Children of the Forest and the First Men was signed here, ending their war.

metadata.description: A mysterious island in the center of the God's Eye, covered in ancient weirwood trees with carved faces, guarded by the Green Men.
metadata.narratorText: The Isle of Faces is one of the last remaining sanctuaries of the Children of the Forest's religion in the south. The faces carved into the weirwoods keep watch over the lake.

metadata.description: A swampy, waterlogged isthmus that connects the North to the south. It is filled with quicksand, alligators, and floating peat bog.
metadata.narratorText: The Neck is a formidable natural defense. It is inhabited by crannogmen, who use guerrilla warfare to annihilate any hostile force trying to march north.

metadata.description: An ancient ring fort built on a steep hill deep in the Haunted Forest, commanding a view of the surrounding wilderness.
metadata.narratorText: The Fist is a natural defensive position used by the First Men thousands of years ago. It stands as a lonely stone crown overlooking the wild forest.

metadata.description: A crude homestead located in the Haunted Forest, inhabited by the wildling Craster and his many wives.
metadata.narratorText: A simple wooden hall and pigsty, Craster's Keep serves as a crucial, if hostile, staging post for Night's Watch rangings north of the Wall.
